0.name: Renfe: high speed, long and medium distance

rules.day: The timetable is that of Wednesday 9 December 2026: the first Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday inside every file, after the day the newest one was written, on which every operator and every Cercanías network runs at least 90% of the trains of its busiest day of the same weekday. The files only overlap from 28 November to 12 December, so that day is compared with 1 other Wednesday. Trains running on from the day before are not counted. Files: Renfe AV/LD, of 27 November 2026; Renfe Cercanías, of 24 November 2026; Ouigo, of 2 July 2026; Iryo, of 5 November 2026.
rules.router: The shortest journey to any station in the municipality of Madrid over all of the day's departures (profile Connection Scan), with at least 10 minutes to change trains and walks of up to 1.5 km in a straight line between stations at 4.5 km/h, also to start the journey at another station nearby. Trains are boarded and left only where the timetable allows it.
rules.access: Each hex adds to the journey of the best station within 30 km of its centre the straight-line distance at 40 km/h, a map convention rather than a driving time. Further away, no value.
rules.trains: A station's trains are the distinct trains that can be boarded there that day; a train the timetable writes several times (once for each stretch where it may be boarded) counts once, at stations and on track. Stations where no train can be boarded that day are not shown.
rules.ghost: OpenStreetMap railways are snapped to links between hexes. Each pair of consecutive stops takes the shortest path along them, if it is at most 1.5 times the straight line plus 15 km, and adds its trains to each link; high-speed and AVANT trains prefer high-speed track (highspeed=yes) and the others conventional track, each link of the other kind counting 2 times its length. A ghost line is Adif track with no passenger train that day; it may carry freight. Not drawn as ghost: track within 10 km of a stop pair with no track path, and stretches of 3 links or fewer beside served track of the same line (OSM ref), which usually are a train counted on the parallel track. Other operators' track without trains is not drawn.

lens.unit: hours and minutes of timetabled travel
lens.description: The shortest train journey to Madrid on Wednesday 9 December 2026, from the best station within 30 km, plus the way there.
lens.note: Timetable of Wednesday 9 December 2026 (week of 7 to 13 December), with every departure of the day. Trains of Renfe, Ouigo and Iryo (Iryo's from an unofficial compilation). Left out: FGC, Euskotren, FGV, SFM, metros, trams and buses. It is the published timetable: delays, sold-out trains and later works are not counted. The straight-line access to the station at 40 km/h, the 30 km radius, the 10 minutes to change trains and the walks of up to 1.5 km between stations are map conventions, not measured times. With the lens on, track with trains is drawn thicker the more trains it carries, and Adif track without passenger trains in dashed grey. 16 pairs of consecutive stops match no OpenStreetMap track: their track is not drawn. The Feve trains in Renfe's high-speed, long and medium-distance file are counted; Renfe Feve's own file is not in the map, so Adif's metre-gauge track with no train in the first is not drawn, even where Feve runs. From 56 stations with trains no journey reaches Madrid that day; among them, those of the R3, whose trains that day only run from La Garriga to La Tor de Querol-Enveig.
